text: Experiment effisql-r1-1-a17c71 (round 1) proposed a verify-before-submit policy: no rewrite submitted until a checksum+count equivalence check against base_sql matches, motivated by four zero-scoring mismatched rewrites (missing subquery columns, union-aggregate type drift, COUNT(l_quantity) vs COUNT(*), LIMIT-tie breakage). The implementer exited at the cost limit, so the change was never implemented and was rejected on implementation failure — this says nothing about whether verification would help, only that the spec (dual checksums, EXCEPT ALL both directions, budget caps, structural-conservative fallbacks) was too large for one implementer round. If retried, strip it to a single cheap verification path (bidirectional EXCEPT ALL plus count equality) and split the rest into smaller separate changes; budget the one base-side run and skip hashing huge outputs like task 6's 4.5M rows.

Experiment effisql-r1-2-5bff70 (round 1) rejected keep-fastest-verified purely for implementation failure: the implementer hit IMPLEMENTER_EXIT_COST_LIMIT and no code landed, so the rejection is weak evidence — it says nothing about the idea's merit. The motivating waste is real in the record: tasks 297 and 225 burned steps on 'cannot insert multiple commands into a prepared statement' errors, and budget exhaustion forced base_sql submission even though known rewrite shapes existed (297 decorrelating the row-constructor scalar subquery into a LEFT JOIN, 44 unnest + array_positions, 130 the HAVING min<>max form). Next time, split the proposal so each piece fits the implementer's cost limit: first the small mechanical fix (one statement per execute_sql call, no re-runs, plain EXPLAIN), then the verified-rewrite registry with the endgame submit-best-at-80%-budget rule, evaluated separately.

Experiment effisql-r1-3-be7f3a (round 1) proposed adding skills/rewrite-shapes.md with four templates (lateral pushdown of an aggregate onto a LIMIT-k set for task 112's 1.19 shape, per-row lateral top-1 via GROUP BY+LIMIT 1 instead of windows for task 119's 1.03, exact COUNT(col) NULL semantics with UNION ALL re-pivot, row-constructor decorrelation), each ending with 'time against base; try next shape under 1.2x'. It was never tested: the implementer exited at IMPLEMENTER_EXIT_COST_LIMIT, so the DECISION_REJECTED for implementation failure is weak evidence against the idea itself. Next time, add skills in smaller slices (one or two templates per round) so writing the file fits the implementer's cost budget, then re-run to actually measure whether the stronger shapes move tau past 1.2 on tasks 112, 119, 225 and 47.

Experiment effisql-r2-2-3f6856 (round 2, shapes-lateral-decorrelate) was rejected for IMPLEMENTER_EXIT_COST_LIMIT — the same failure as round 1's version of skills/rewrite-shapes.md. Shrinking the skill to two templates with no task-specific SQL was still too expensive for the implementer, so evidence now says even a minimal new skill file exceeds the cost budget; a third attempt should be drastically smaller (one template, or a few lines appended to an existing file) or use a cheaper channel. Because nothing executed, this rejection says nothing about the technical merit: top-k-then-LATERAL (task 112) and decorrelate-to-join (tasks 119, 297) remain untested and worth a cheaper retry. The separately noted verification rule (submit base_sql when tau < 1) is still the cheapest fix for tasks 47/71, which scored below identity; 169/225 sit near a scan floor and need different shapes.

Experiment effisql-r3-1-650304 rejected verify-eq-gate-v2 for IMPLEMENTATION_FAILED: the implementer hit its step limit even on the 'slim' one-statement EXCEPT ALL gate, echoing round 1's effisql-r1-1 which also died on implementer cost. Two consecutive implementation failures are weak evidence against the hypothesis itself — the diagnosis that tasks 6, 113, 185 and 203 each lost 0.25-0.5 to unchecked non-equivalent rewrites (dropped column, SUM type drift, COUNT semantics, LIMIT 1 tie-break) stands untested — but strong evidence that any multi-part policy.py edit (SQL template plus budget check plus fallback branch) exceeds the implementer's step budget. Next time: do not retry the same shape a third time; stage it across rounds (one round just the fixed SQL string constant, the next the wiring), or fold the check into an existing decision point instead of adding a new rule branch. Track implementer step usage before proposing.

Experiment effisql-r3-2-0c226d (round 3): the speed-gate-and-step-hygiene change to policy.py — submit only rewrites timed at ≥1.2x via one EXPLAIN ANALYZE, one statement per execute_sql call, never re-run known results — was rejected (REJECTION_REASON_IMPLEMENTATION_FAILED) because the implementer hit IMPLEMENTER_EXIT_STEP_LIMIT; the hypothesis itself was never tested. This is the second step-limit failure in this idea family (round 1's keep-fastest-verified failed only on implementer cost), so even the split-out 'mechanical half' (no registry, no endgame code) was too large for one implementer run. Next time: slice even smaller (the gate alone, then hygiene rules), pre-draft the exact patch text so the implementer only applies and verifies it, or raise the implementer step limit. The credit argument (identity tau~1, credit 0.5 beats a 0.94-1.1x rewrite at 0.25) remains plausible but unvalidated.

effisql-r3-3-1a675e (prompt-only half of rejected effisql-r1-1-a17c71) appended an ~8-line pre-submit equivalence checklist to prompt.md: keep computed columns from flattened subqueries, COUNT(col) non-NULL semantics, NULL-vs-zero, UNION ALL ::numeric casts, tied ORDER BY under LIMIT. Guards passed and screening gained +5.6 R-VES (9 tasks, 1 seed), but validation failed: -0.9 vs +10 needed over 28 tasks, one regression, wall time 1.64x tripping the cost guardrail, and one prediction flagged hard-coded/literal_result. The no-gain verdict is weak evidence (p=0.5 in both splits; the 9-task screening delta didn't transfer), but the hard-code flag is strong evidence of harm — mechanism unclear, possibly the 'confirm the exact row matches' wording nudging literal outputs. Don't resubmit prompt-only checklists; equivalence safety needs a mechanized verify/fallback gate. Prompt additions also inflate runtime (tokens 1.29x).

effisql-r5-3-96671c, third try at a top-k-LATERAL skill (r1/r2 versions died on implementer cost): one 12-line template, submitted cleanly, all guards passed. Screen passed (+4.5 on 11 tasks) but validation gave only +0.9 R-VES vs 10.0 needed, 1 win/1 loss, p=0.750, and the cost guardrail tripped (tokens 1.37x, wall time 2.26x): the implementer inlined the skill into prompt.md because pack code may open no file, so every task now pays the extra prompt tokens. Two lessons: count how many pool tasks actually match a shape before writing a skill for it (this shape is ~1 in 28, so even a perfect fix cannot reach significance), and prompt.md inlining makes skill cost per-task and scaling with prompt size — the 2.26x wall-time trip is concrete evidence, unlike the 1-seed significance rejection, which is weak. Retire topk-lateral at the skill level.
